title: The Apostolic Planting and Forged Epistles
english: Having been made a planting from Peter and Paul, you harvested both Romans and Corinthians. For both of them, having planted us even into our own Corinth, taught identically.
And having taught together in Italy likewise, they were martyred at the same time. And the same [person] says these things concerning his own letters, as having been tampered with.

For I wrote letters at the request of brothers who asked me to write. And the apostles of the devil have filled these with weeds: some things they take away, and some things they add; to which the 'woe' lies. It is no wonder, then, if some have attempted to tamper even with the Lord's scriptures, since they have laid their plots against those not of such a kind.

And first it must be said concerning Dionysius: that he had been entrusted with the throne of the episcopate of the sojourning in Corinth; and how, of the divine philanthropy, he shared abundantly not only with those under him, but already also with those in foreign lands; most useful...

title: Description of the Epistles
english: Having made himself known to all, in which he represented himself through universal letters to the churches. Of these, the one to the Lacedaemonians is catechetical regarding orthodoxy, and foundational for peace and unity.

The one to the Athenians is an awakening of faith and of the way of life according to the Gospel; which, having grown small, he reproves, saying that they must be little ones departing from the Word, from which it came about that their leader Publius was martyred in the persecutions of that time. And he mentions Quadratus having become their bishop after the martyred Publius; testifying how, through his zeal, they had been gathered together and had received a rekindling of faith.

And he shows upon this, how even Dionysius the Areopagite, having been turned to faith by the apostle Paul according to what was made manifest in the deeds [Acts 17:34], was first entrusted with the oversight of the residence in Athens.

title: Summary of Letters
english: Having sent letters to the sojourning communities in Crete, he approves Philip as their bishop, since the church under him was being attested for very many noble deeds; and he reminds them to guard against the perversion of the heretics.

And regarding the church residing in Amastris, he sent letters to them by way of Pontus, and he remembers having urged Bakchylides and Elpis to write to him; he sets forth explanations of divine writings; he marks out Palman as their bishop; and he advises the same people much concerning marriage and chastity. He also commands that those who are turning back from whatever fall, whether from fault or from heretical error, should be received.

By these [means] another letter was sent toward the Knossians, in which he exhorts Pinutos, the bishop of the resident aliens, not to lay the heavy burden concerning chastity upon the brothers as compulsory, but to have regard for the weakness of the many.

And another letter of Dionysius is brought alongside these, having been sent to a most faithful sister, Chrysophoros. In which, by writing the appropriate things, she also shared in the logical food that was fitting for her.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
